chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from Abi al-Mi'za, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who recites the Surah of those who disbelieved will never waver, and doubt will never enter his religion, and Allah will never afflict him with poverty, nor fear from the ruler, and he will remain protected from doubt and disbelief until he dies. When he dies, Allah will appoint for him in his grave a thousand angels who pray in his grave, and the reward of their prayers will be for him, and they will escort him until they present him in a position of safety before Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and he will be in the safety of Allah and the safety of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.سُورَهَ الَّذِینَ کَفَرُوا: Surah of those who disbelieved (referring to Surah Muhammad or Surah Al-Kafirun)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and protections for reciting Surah Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith links the recitation of Surah Muhammad (specifically the opening verses addressing the disbelievers) to comprehensive divine protection, promising immunity from doubt, poverty, and fear of rulers. It further emphasizes the eschatological reward of a thousand angels praying in the grave, ensuring the reciter’s safe presentation before God. This reflects the Shia tradition of viewing specific Quranic recitations as means to secure both worldly stability and spiritual assurance in the afterlife.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan from Abi al-Mi’za from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

One who recites it, doubt will never enter his religion, and protection from polytheism and disbelief will never leave him till he dies. Then when he dies, Allah appoints for him in his grave a thousand angels that pray in his grave, and the reward of their prayers will be for him, and they will remain with him till he is presented in a calm and quiet atmosphere before Allah, and he will be in the safety of Allah and safety of Muhammad (s.a.w.s.).
